Attention Trading Partners: MIHMS Upgrade October Payment Cycle Changes and System Access Limitations

Sep 28, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) is preparing to launch an upgraded version of MIHMS, MaineCare’s claims processing system. The upgrade is currently scheduled to go live on October 10, 2026. To support a smooth transition, OMS must implement temporary system access limitations and adjustments to payment cycles in October.  

From Friday, October 2 at 8:00 PM until Monday, October 12 at 8:00 AM, MIHMS will be in a “data freeze” while OMS completes final system readiness and transition activities. 

Please note that we have updated the FAQ previously shared, as of September 21, 2026. 

Changes to October payment cycles: 

Review this information and plan billing accordingly to prepare for the transition.    

Payment Cycle Date 

Type of Cycle 

Claim Submission Deadline for Inclusion in Payment Cycle* 

Wednesday, 9/30/26  

Last regular payment cycle before the data freeze  

Friday, 9/25/26, 5:00 AM 

Thursday, 10/1/26 

Extra payment cycle before the data freeze 

Wednesday, 9/30/26, 5:00 AM 

There will be no payment on Wednesday, October 7. 

Thursday, 10/15/26 

First payment cycle after data freeze, in upgraded system 

Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) submission: Continuous through data freeze up to Tuesday, 10/13/26, 2:00 PM 

  

Portal submission: 

Before data freeze: Friday, 10/2/26, 7:59 PM 

After data freeze: Tuesday, 10/13/26, 2:00 PM 

Wednesday, 10/21/26 

Regular payment cycle, in upgraded system 

Friday, 10/16/26, 5:00 AM 

*As always, timely submission does not guarantee that the claim will process in time for the next payment cycle. OMS may take up to 30 days to process and pay a claim, depending on any edits or issues that may cause the claim to pend for manual review, as well as other processing requirements that may require the full 30-day timeframe. 

Preparing for the changes to October payment cycles: 

The HealthPAS Online Portal has returned to its previous regular operating hours. Providers again have 24/7 access to the portal, for additional flexibility and time to submit claims outside of standard business hours.   

We strongly encourage providers to submit claims approaching timely filing limits in the next few weeks to avoid potential submission delays. The planned data freeze does not modify existing Medicaid timely filing requirements. Providers remain responsible for ensuring claims are submitted within the established timely filing guidelines. 

Other system access limitations: 

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. We have updated the FAQ as of September 21, 2026. Topics include: 

  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility 
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA) 
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal 
  • Paper & fax document submissions 
  • Provider Services & Member Services call centers 
  • Value Added Network (VAN) Trading Partners 
  • Prior authorizations for prescriptions and behavioral health services 
  • Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) 
  • Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) 

You can also check the OMS Provider Resources webpage, in the first box of information called “Health PAS Online Portal,” for the most recent information about the upgrade.  

For questions or clarifications, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. Please note, Provider Services does not have additional information beyond what is shared in this message and in the FAQ linked above.

Attention Trading Partners: Refresher Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 28, 2026

As a reminder, the new MaineCare Partner Portal is scheduled to go live on October 12, 2026, at 8:00 AM. The new portal will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal and provide enhanced functionality to support Trading Partner operations. We are adding additional live, virtual instructor-led training sessions to help Trading Partners prepare for the transition. 

As a reminder, recorded training sessions, training materials, user guides, Q&A documents from training sessions, and supporting resources are available through the MMIS Learning Center and will continue to be available after go-live. 

Please share this training information with staff responsible for claims, authorizations, referrals, account maintenance, and portal administration activities. Staff should not wait for refresher training to become familiar with the materials. 

Key Reminders

  • Trading Partner Administrator (R7) accounts will be migrated to the new portal. 
  • Additional users will be invited and managed by Trading Partner Administrators after go-live. 
  • Trading Partner Administrators (R7 users) should prepare for portal access and account setup activities by reviewing the training materials available in the MMIS Learning Center before go-live.

entry.title: Disability Employment Awareness Month - October
entry.content:
WHEREAS, October 2026 marks the 81st anniversary of National Disability Employment Awareness Month; and

WHEREAS, workplaces across our state that are welcoming of the talents of all people, including people with disabilities, are critical to healthy communities and a strong economy; and

WHEREAS, while the employment rate of people with disabilities ages 16 to 64 in Maine has increased to 44 percent, it remains significantly lower than the 83 percent employment rate for Maine people without disabilities; and

WHEREAS, it is important that the State of Maine prepare all youth, including those with disabilities, for meaningful careers and an adulthood that includes employment; and

WHEREAS, Maine is an Employment First state, affirming employment as the first and preferred option for people with disabilities who receive services from state agencies; and

WHEREAS, people with disabilities, including people who are Deaf, Hard of Hearing, Late Deafened, Blind or with Low Vision make significant contributions to Maine's economy and communities; and

WHEREAS, activities during this month will reinforce the value and talent people with disabilities add to our workplaces and communities and affirm Maine's commitment to increasing access to good jobs and competitive, integrated employment for all workers, including those with disabilities;

NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim October 2026 as 

Disability Employment Awareness Month

throughout the State of Maine, and I call upon employers, schools, higher education institutions and other community organizations in Maine to observe October with appropriate programs and activities that celebrate the contributions of people with disabilities and promote access to good, in-demand jobs and career pathways such as registered apprenticeships for all Maine people.

In testimony whereof, I have caused

the Great Seal of the State to be

hereunto affixed GIVEN under my

hand at Augusta this twenty eighth day of

September Two Thousand Twenty-Six

entry.title: Domestic Violence Awareness Month - October
entry.content:
WHEREAS, domestic abuse and violence is a serious injustice and public health crisis that affects people and families of all races, ages, genders, sexual orientations, and income levels; and

WHEREAS, each year nearly half of all homicides in Maine are related to domestic abuse and violence; and

WHEREAS, support and help are available 24/7/365 to anyone affected by domestic abuse, through the programs of the Maine Coalition to End Domestic Violence and the statewide domestic violence helpline; and

WHEREAS, domestic abuse and violence is entirely preventable, and all Maine people have opportunities to intervene and change the ways we and our communities understand and act on the issue of domestic abuse and violence; and 

WHEREAS, community leaders are uniquely positioned to make a broad and lasting impact by enacting policies and practices that support survivors and their children, and hold abusive people to account; 

NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim October 2026 as

Domestic Violence Awareness Month

throughout the State of Maine, and I urge all citizens to recognize this observance.

hereunto affixed GIVEN under my

hand at Augusta this twenty eighth day of

entry.title: National PA Week - October 6 through 12
entry.content:
WHEREAS, quality, cost-effective, and patient-centered healthcare is essential to the well-being and quality of life of all people in Maine; and


WHEREAS, physician associates/assistants (PAs) are nationally certified and state-licensed medical professionals who diagnose illnesses, develop and manage treatment plans, prescribe medications, and often serve as a patient's principal healthcare provider; and


WHEREAS, PAs are trusted providers and vital members of the healthcare team, enhancing access to high-quality care in primary care settings, hospitals, rural communities, and underserved areas; and
 

WHEREAS, PAs deliver compassionate, expert care, often serving as the first point of contact for patients and empowering individuals and families to be active participants in their own health; and
 

WHEREAS, PAs provide critical care across a broad range of medical specialties, including addressing the growing demand for behavioral and mental health services by offering compassionate, evidence-based care to individuals and families in need; and
 

WHEREAS, PAs are committed to addressing health disparities, expanding access, and providing team-based, person-centered care across every medical specialty and setting; and
 

WHEREAS, PAs have earned the respect of patients and colleagues alike for their clinical excellence, adaptability, and deep dedication to the communities they serve; and
 

WHEREAS, Maine has been a leader in progressing PA practice and ensuring access to PA services by enacting legislation in recent years to join the PA compact, change the title of the profession to accurately reflect the scope of the profession, and allow PAs to practice at the top of their education and training;


NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim October 6-12, 2026 as 

National PA Week

in Maine, and I encourage all residents to recognize and celebrate the important role that PAs play in improving health, advancing equity, and delivering high-quality care across the healthcare system.

hereunto affixed GIVEN under my

entry.title: US Labor Department obtains court order naming independent fiduciary for 401(k) plan of defunct WA-based aerospace company
entry.content: SEATTLE – The U.S. Department of Labor has secured a court order to appoint an independent fiduciary to manage the abandoned 401(k) plan of a defunct Arlington-based aerospace company.The order, entered in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington, appoints AMI Benefit Plan Administrators Inc. as the independent fiduciary for the Commercial Aircraft Interiors LLC 401(k) Plan, which has been frozen since the employer shut down operations in 2023. In this role, the independent fiduciary will be able to distribute its assets to eligible former employees who have not been able to access their retirement savings because the only responsive company representative, Charles Pratt, lacked the legal authority needed to approve distributions. The independent fiduciary will also be able to formally terminate the plan.“The appointment of an independent fiduciary will give the participants in the Commercial Aircraft Interiors plan access to the funds that rightly belong to them,” said Liam Roberts, district director for the department’s Employee Benefits Security Administration in Seattle. “We urge all workers to contact the department for assistance when their retirement plan has been abandoned and they have not received the benefits to which they are entitled.”Under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act, all employee benefit plans are required to be managed by named fiduciaries. Without one, participants and beneficiaries cannot get information about their accounts or collect retirement benefits. The Commercial Aircraft Interiors plan has approximately $260,000 in assets and 59 participants.EBSA ensures the security of retirement, health, and other job-based benefits for American workers and their families. The agency is responsible for protecting more than 155 million workers, retirees, and their families, who are covered by approximately 2.8 million health plans, 837,000 private retirement plans, and 521,000 additional welfare benefit plans. Together, these plans hold about $15.2 trillion in assets.Employers and workers can contact EBSA at askebsa.dol.gov or call 866-444-3272 toll-free for help with private sector job-based retirement and health plans.

entry.title: Former union officials charged with wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud for embezzling approximately $350K in member funds over 5 years
entry.content: CLEVELAND – An investigation by the U.S. Department of Labor has led to criminal charges for two former union officials who allegedly embezzled approximately $350,000 from the union members they swore to serve.An investigation by the department’s Office of Labor-Management Standards in Cleveland found that the former president and secretary-treasurer of the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees Local 1746 conspired to access the union’s finances for unauthorized transactions for their personal benefit from 2017 to 2022.Criminal charges were filed this month in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio against the union’s former President Pamela Brown and former Secretary-Treasurer Adelle Burrell-Williams. The charging documents allege these former officers used the union’s debit card to withdraw cash at casinos and wrote unauthorized checks from the union’s operating account. The department also alleges that Brown and Burrell-Williams attempted to avoid detection by creating false reports and failing to maintain financial records. The union lost approximately $350,000 as a result of Brown and Burrell-Williams’ actions. The former union officials were responsible for overseeing the union, managing its finances, paying authorized expenses, maintaining financial records, and creating financial reports during their tenures as principal officers of Local 1746, a union representing 1,200 employees at Cuyahoga County Health and Human Services.The prosecution of this case is being handled by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio.Criminal complaints, or the filing of an information, are charges only and are not evidence of guilt. Each defendant is entitled to a fair trial in which it is the government’s burden to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. Labor union fraud such as embezzlement, filing false reports, maintaining false records, destroying or concealing records, and other criminal activity can be reported by email to OLMS-Public@dol.gov, to the OLMS National Office at 202-693-0143, or to your local OLMS field office. MaineCare in Education: Updated Joint Individual Education Program (IEP) Guidance for School Health-Related Services

Oct 01, 2026

As a reminder, all providers who deliver services following the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) must ensure all MaineCare-covered services are documented following the Department of Health and Human Services/Maine Department of Education Joint IEP Guidance document. 

The Maine Department of Education has released updated Joint IEP Guidance to help schools follow federal and state requirements. The updated guidance was developed through a collaborative effort and is available on the MaineCare in Education web page. 

DOE first released the Joint Guidance on August 28, 2026, and has re-issued this guidance effective September 18, 2026. The reissued guidance replaces the previously issued Joint Guidance and provides clarification in response to questions and feedback received from School Administrative Units (SAUs), providers, and other interested parties. 

All IEP documents must reflect the updated guidance as soon as possible, but no later than thirty (30) days of the issuance of the guidance. 

Providers with current prior authorizations for School Health-Related Services through Acentra should upload any updated documentation to Atrezzo. Acentra will accept IEP language from both versions through October 18, 2026. Beginning October 19, 2026, Acentra will only accept IEP language from the new version re-issued on September 18, 2026.

Actuarial report projects PFML Trust Fund will remain stable for the next 10 years

AUGUSTA - The Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) program has published its second annual actuarial report, as well as its first claims report on Oct. 1, 2026.

PFML became law in 2023 and is a statewide program that provides eligible workers with up to 12 weeks of paid leave for medical, parental, family care, military family or safe leave.

This initial claims report covers the program's first three months of claims activity, from March 30 through June 30, 2026. Future claims reports will be published annually and will cover a full year of claims activity.

  • The PFML Trust Fund remains solvent and based on updated revenue and claim expenditure, is projected to remain stable for the next 10 years.
  • The program received 8,376 applications between March 30 and June 30, 2026.
  • Among the claims approved, medical leave was the most common reason, followed by welcoming a new child and caring for a family member. Other leave reasons represented a very small portion of the overall claim volume.

"We are excited to see the PFML Program effectively off the ground and helping Maine workers and businesses through life's big moments, both now and for years to come," said PFML Director Luke Monahan.

entry.title: US Labor Department finds railroad illegally terminated employee who refused to work during severe weather
entry.content: LITTLE ROCK, AR – A U.S. Department of Labor Occupational Safety and Health Administration whistleblower investigation has concluded that Union Pacific Railroad Co. violated the Federal Railroad Safety Act when it removed from service and later terminated a North Little Rock yardman who notified management of nearby lightning and federal safety standards. OSHA determined that the employee voiced concerns about nearby lightning, cited OSHA and NOAA lightening safety guidelines, initiated a safety stand-down, and refused to work until the storm passed. Within minutes of the stand-down, Union Pacific removed the employee from service and was later charged with insubordination. Union Pacific terminated his employment on May 30, 2024.On June 10, 2026, OSHA ordered Union Pacific to remove from the employee’s employment records any reference of the incident, and pay back wages, lost benefits, compensatory and punitive damages totaling at least $304,869, and attorney’s fees. Union Pacific filed objections to OSHA’s order and has requested a hearing before a U.S. Department of Labor Administrative Law Judge.OSHA’s Whistleblower Protection Program enforces 25 whistleblower statutes that protect employees from retaliation for reporting violations of workplace airline, anti-money laundering, commercial motor carrier, consumer product, criminal antitrust, environmental, financial reform, food safety, health insurance reform, maritime, motor vehicle safety, nuclear, pipeline, public transportation agency, railroad, safety and health, securities, and tax laws.Editor’s note: The U.S. Department of Labor does not release the names of employees involved in whistleblower complaints.

entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration today announced the award approximately $10.2 million in grant funds to 67 organizations across the nation to support education and training focused on worker safety to help employees and employers recognize serious workplace hazards and employ safety and health programs.Funded through the Susan Harwood Training Grant Program, the grants aim to advance worker safety and health by providing instructor-led training opportunities for workers and employers in small businesses with an emphasis on industries with high injury, illness, and fatality rates.The grants will fund training and education on hazard awareness, prevention, and controls to protect workers from on-the-job hazards through the development of quality classroom-ready training and educational materials that identify and prevent workplace hazards.The grants honor the legacy and work of Dr. Susan Harwood who, during her 17 years with OSHA, developed workplace safety guidelines for benzene, formaldehyde, bloodborne pathogens and lead in the construction industry. As a reminder, all providers delivering telehealth services to MaineCare members must be enrolled with MaineCare and must comply with MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) Chapter I, Section 4: Telehealth Services.  

Chapter I, Section 4 requires that providers be “appropriately licensed, accredited, certified, and/or registered in the state where the member is located during the provision of the telehealth service.”

entry.title: Maine CDC Encourages Tick Bite Prevention This Fall
entry.content:
Oct 05, 2026

Reminds Maine people and visitors ticks remain active even as temperatures fall

As days get shorter and leaves begin to change, ticks remain active across Maine. The Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC) urges all Maine people and visitors to protect themselves from tick bites this fall.

Ticks can be active throughout the fall and during winter days, whenever temperatures rise above freezing. Fall is a busy time for outdoor activities, bringing people into contact with ticks more often. People may encounter them during everyday fall activities, like cleaning the yard or hunting.

Current year preliminary counts from the Maine Tracking Network show that health care providers reported over 5,000 cases of tickborne disease so far this year. This includes diseases like Lyme disease, anaplasmosis, and babesiosis.

“Many people think ticks are only a summer problem, but ticks can remain active throughout the fall,” said Maine CDC Director Puthiery Va. “You can enjoy Maine’s beautiful fall weather and outdoor activities while staying safe by taking a few simple steps before, during, and after can help protect you from tickborne disease.”

Ticks often live in wooded and brushy areas and areas with leaf litter. The Maine CDC encourages everyone to think TICKS when spending time outdoors: 

  • T – Take an EPA-approved repellent and use it before going outside. Use DEET, picaridin, IR3535, or oil of lemon eucalyptus on skin. Pre-treat clothing with permethrin.
  • I – Inspect your body daily. Check yourself, children, and pets for ticks after spending time outdoors.
  • C – Cover your skin. Wear long-sleeved shirts and long pants and tuck pants into socks. Light-colored clothing makes ticks easier to spot.
  • K – Know your surroundings. Be aware when you are in tick habitat and take extra precautions.
  • S – Shower after being outdoors. Showering helps wash off ticks before they attach. Put clothes in the dryer on high heat for at least 15 minutes before washing to kill ticks.

Remember to check for ticks after any outdoor activity and before bed each night. Check in areas where ticks may be easy to miss, including the scalp, behind the ears, under the arms, around the waist, between the legs, and behind the knees.

The most common symptoms of tickborne disease include flu-like symptoms. People who have Lyme disease may also find an expanding rash somewhere on their body. This rash can sometimes, though not always, look like a bullseye. If you experience any of these symptoms, talk to a health care provider and be sure to mention any recent tick exposure.

The University of Maine Cooperative Extension Tick Lab offers tick identification for free and tick testing to Maine residents for a $20 fee. Testing can take up to three days and should be used for surveillance purposes only, not for diagnosis. Finding a tick on you, even if it was attached, does not necessarily mean that it spread any germs to you. Find more information at ticks.umaine.edu. 

To learn more about how to stay tick free, visit the Maine CDC's website.

Maine Senate Confirms Vaughan Woodruff as Chair of the State Workforce Development Board

October 5, 2026

For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Maine Senate confirmed Vaughan Woodruff, principal of EquinoxDG, to a second term as chair of the State Workforce Development Board (SWDB). Gov. Janet Mills announced her nomination of Woodruff on Sept. 8, 2026. Woodruff has served as chair of the SWDB since 2023.

Prior to founding EquinoxDG, Woodruff was vice president of regulatory reform at the Interstate Renewable Energy Council and vice president of workforce development and interconnection strategy at ReVision Energy, where he oversaw the company's long-term strategic vision for training and talent development and developed nationally recognized registered apprenticeships in clean energy.

"The State Workforce Development Board plays a critical role in coordinating Maine's workforce development efforts to support economic growth and address workforce challenges," said Maine Department of Labor Commissioner Laura Fortman. "Vaughan Woodruff is a well-respected business leader with deep workforce expertise. His continued leadership will help maintain momentum as we strengthen Maine's workforce and economy."

"I appreciate the trust that Gov. Mills and the Maine Senate have placed in me through my nomination and confirmation to continue serving the people of Maine in this role," said Woodruff. "I feel privileged to work with the outstanding staff and members of the Board to increase the accessibility of the workforce system to Maine workers and businesses and to proactively address the workforce challenges ahead of us."

Woodruff is a seventh-generation Maine native who was raised in Pittsfield. He earned a bachelor's degree in civil engineering from the University of Maine and a master's degree in education from Prescott College in Arizona. Woodruff was the founder and CEO of Insource Renewables, an employee-owned solar company that was recognized as a Best for the World for Workers company by B Lab prior to its acquisition by ReVision Energy in 2021.

During Woodruff's tenure as chair, the SWDB has:

  • Launched Work Source Maine, the state's online resource connecting job seekers, students, parents, educators, career counselors and employers with resources to explore, plan and achieve career and workforce goals;

  • Launched the Maine Workforce Pell program, which expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term, career-focused training programs that deliver industry-recognized credentials and measurable employment results, preparing students for in-demand occupations; and

  • Secured $15M+ in funding to support industry partnerships in advanced manufacturing, forest bioproducts and defense, and expand career exploration, job supports, and upskilling investments including registered pre-apprenticeships

As chair, Woodruff will continue to work with the SWDB, state agencies, education and training providers, employers and other partners to strengthen Maine's workforce development system and help connect Maine people with career opportunities.

Woodruff serves on the Electrical Technologies Advisory Committee at Kennebec Valley Community College and previously served on the Western Mountains Committee of the Maine Community Foundation and the Pittsfield Planning Board. Woodruff lives in Pittsfield with his wife, Holly Zadra, and their two sons, Eamon and Goran.

New MaineCare Partner Portal: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Requirements

Oct 06, 2026

As a reminder, the new MaineCare Partner Portal is scheduled to go live on October 12, 2026, at 8:00 AM. The new portal will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal and will require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). Read below for more information and steps you will need to take to sign into the MaineCare Partner Portal starting on October 12. 

For all information about the upcoming changes to MIHMS, see the “HealthPAS Online Portal” section of the Provider Resources page.  

Multi-Factor Authenticator (MFA) 

MFA adds a second verification step after entering your password. This is an important new security measure to protect the sensitive information held in the Portal. You will have three options to choose from for your additional authentication factor; you must choose one.

Follow the instructions below for first-time setup of the option you choose. 

  1. Microsoft Authenticator 

The Microsoft Authenticator app is the recommended MFA method because it offers the highest level of protection over other methods. Download the Microsoft Authenticator app now on a smartphone or tablet so that you are ready to use it on October 12. 

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via the app:  

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Open the Microsoft Authenticator app. 
  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Click the QR code scanner in the Microsoft Authenticator app and scan the QR code displayed on the Portal’s User Details window.  

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process.

 

  1. Text/Call 

Text (SMS) or call verification is available as an MFA option through September 2027.  

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via text (SMS) or call: 

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Select the “Text/call” option then click “Continue.” 
  • Enter a phone number, request a code or call, then verify the code. The phone number you provide during setup will be saved as your registered MFA contact method and will be used for future authentication and account verification activities. 

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process.

 

  1. Email 

Email verification is available as an MFA option through September 2027. 

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via email: 

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Select the “Email” option then click “Continue.” 
  • Enter an email address, request a code, then verify the code. The email address you provide during setup will be saved as your registered MFA contact method and will be used for future authentication and account verification activities. 

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process. 

 

For additional instructions on both initial setup and ongoing use of MFA, including screenshots, please reference the job aid MaineCare Partner Portal MFA Setup and Access Job Aid. 

  • You can find this job aid and other supporting resources through the MMIS Learning Center. Search for the course “ME – MIHMS Upgrade Documentation,” enroll in the course, then look for the job aid in the documentation list.

Thank you for preparing in advance for a smooth transition to the new MaineCare Partner Portal.

entry.title: US Department of Labor cites Pennsylvania excavation employer for failing to provide trench protection following fatal trench cave-in
entry.content: CHAMBERSBURG, PA – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited an excavation contractor for willful and serious safety violations after a young worker was fatally injured in a trench collapse. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration opened an investigation into Jonas David Wagoner – doing business as J.D. Wagoner Excavating – on April 2, 2026, and found workers were installing a storm sewer system 12 feet below ground level in a trench that was not adequately protected from soil collapse. When a portion of the trench's wall failed, the unrestrained soil engulfed one worker. The agency issued a willful violation for failure to protect workers from cave-ins and two repeat violations for failing to assign a competent person to conduct daily trench inspections and removing employees from hazardous conditions.In addition, the employer received three serious violations for failure to provide construction hazard prevention training to employees, establish a safe means for workers to exit the excavation site, keep materials at least two feet from the edge of an excavation site, and restrain side materials from becoming roll-in hazards. OSHA proposed $254,884 in penalties. The employer has 15 business days from receiving receipt of its citations and penalties to request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

entry.title: Saving Money on Winter Heating Costs
entry.content:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Well, it's getting more and more painful to fill up at a gas station or fill a tank of oil to heat your home. And we all know why.

Look, we're making progress shifting to other sources of energy to heat our homes, but we're still the most dependent on heating oil to heat our homes in the in the entire country. That reliance on heating oil makes us vulnerable to great shifts in global energy markets that drive up costs for Maine people and businesses. This president's war in Iran right now has created the largest fuel supply disruption in global history and has driven energy prices to record highs. The price of heating oil in Maine has reached more than $6 a gallon, so you'll be paying almost $800 more to fill a standard 275 gallon tank than you did a year ago. Kerosene prices are also reaching historic highs, all because of this war.

Maine people should not be forced to choose between staying warm or putting food on the table because the president chose to drag us into a needless war -- and an endless war, it appears.

My administration is doing what it can to help people save money on heating costs and stay comfortable in their homes this winter.

It's not enough, but I've directed the Department of Health and Human Services to identify households that would be eligible for $40 million in discounts on their electric bills through Maine's Low Income Assistance Program, or LIAP. Starting in November, thousands of eligible families who are customers of CMP or Versant will begin to see discounts ranging from 20 percent to 80 percent, and these will be applied automatically every month to their electric bills. It's one thing we can do. Families who already get federal assistance for home heating oil through LIHEAP, the Low Income Energy Assistance Program, will also be enrolled automatically in this state assistance program, LIAP, to get the maximum savings on their electric bills without any unnecessary paperwork. Customers with questions about this discount should contact their electric company directly.

I've also called on Congress to increase funding for federal home heating assistance, and I thank Maine's congressional delegation for their bipartisan support for LIHEAP funding, despite the president's attempts to eliminate this program. And that's just not enough, though, to make up for the skyrocketing costs driven by tariffs and the president's war. Congress must ensure the safety and comfort of Maine people heading into this winter season by increasing LIHEAP funding.

In the meantime, MaineHousing has distributed about $4 million to heating fuel companies for some of our most vulnerable households, those with older adults on small incomes or small children. Those trucks will begin delivering fuel to those homes over the next few days. We're also talking to farmers and foresters and other entities that use diesel fuel a lot about other ways we might be able to help them address high diesel prices here in Maine.

I'm proud to say that thanks to our investments over the years in energy efficiency and clean energy, our reliance on heating oil has fallen from 70 percent of Maine households in 2010 to just over 50 percent now. Still, it's not enough. My administration will continue to make it as affordable as possible to transition to clean energy sources like heat pumps, to save people money, and to make sure we're not left to shoulder the burden of the president's blunders.

Are you interested in exploring heat pumps or using wood or propane to heat your home instead of oil and kerosene? Are you curious about energy assistance programs? Weatherization? Do you need contact information for local community action agencies or MaineHousing or Efficiency Maine Trust? Our Winter Heating Guide, published every year by the Maine Department of Energy Resources, has all that information, as well as some helpful tips about winterizing and saving money, and about contact information, and links to online resources. You can view and download that Winter Heating Guide and review the latest heating fuel prices at Maine.gov/Energy.

This crisis affects all of us – low income, middle income, everyone who has a home, everyone who has a bill to pay this winter. But as the weather continues to get colder, I encourage all Maine people to see how they might save money and stay warm through the winter by using our current Maine Winter heating guide found at Maine.gov/Energy.

This is Governor Janet Mills. Please stay warm, and thank you for listening.

MaineCare Coverage of Gender-Affirming Care for Medicaid Beneficiaries Under Age 18 and Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) Enrollees Under Age 19

Oct 09, 2026

As described in the message sent September 18, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) published a final rule in the Federal Register on August 13, 2026, that limits federal Medicaid and CHIP funding for certain gender-affirming care provided to minors. This rule prohibits federal matching funds for puberty blockers, cross-sex hormone therapy, and surgical interventions when used for gender transition for Medicaid beneficiaries under age 18 and CHIP enrollees under age 19. The federal rule is scheduled to take effect on October 13, 2026. 

The federal rule does not prohibit states from using state-only funds to cover these services. Maine law requires MaineCare to cover medically necessary treatment for or related to gender dysphoria and protects members from discrimination based on gender identity or gender expression.   

To ensure we are in compliance with this new federal rule, we have established the billing requirements below for providers who deliver gender-affirming care services to Medicaid beneficiaries under age 18 and CHIP enrollees under age 19. 

Effective on October 13, 2026, medical claims submitted through the MIHMS system must: 

  • Include applicable gender-affirming care diagnosis codes on all claims. 
  • Include the SE modifier on any claims submitted for gender-affirming care, other than behavioral health services.  
    • The SE modifier is used to identify a service that must be reimbursed using state-only funds.  
    • The SE modifier should be listed after any other modifiers on the applicable claim line(s). 
    • Behavioral health treatment for gender dysphoria is still eligible for federal match, so providers are not required to include the SE modifier on behavioral health-related claims.  

Effective on October 9, 2026, pharmacy claims submitted through the MEPOPS system must:  

  • Have Prior Authorization (PA) as required on the Department’s Preferred Drug List. This requirement applies to preferred and non-preferred products on the Department’s identified medication list.   
  • Include the medication’s intended clinical use by including the applicable diagnosis code and the information needed to determine the appropriate coverage and funding pathway.  
    • Medication prescribed for a clinical use outside the scope of 42 CFR § 441.801–441.802 and 457.476 remains subject to the otherwise applicable MaineCare pharmacy criteria. For medication prescribed for use within the scope of those provisions, the Department will review coverage under its separately funded state-only benefit.  

This PA requirement is used to determine clinical purpose and payment source. It does not, by itself, change the drug’s preferred status, establish additional step therapy, or mean that all uses of the medication are excluded from federally matched coverage. Existing drug-specific clinical criteria continue to apply as appropriate.  

For questions, please contact Provider Relations Specialist, Lisa Bouchard.

School Health-Related Services: Recommended Draft Rates, Presented Materials, and Comment Deadline

Oct 09, 2026

On October 9, 2026, MaineCare held an online public meeting to present recommended draft rates and assumptions along with detailed rate exhibits for school health-related services. The PowerPoint presentation and video recording of the meeting are available on our MaineCare Rate System Reform webpage.

As providers and other interested parties, your feedback is important. We encourage your participation. The Department will accept written comments on these recommendations through the deadline of October 23, 2026. Please submit comments directly to our vendor Milliman Inc.

The Department will summarize all comments and include an explanation of whether and how we incorporated the feedback into the final rate determination.

Please contact Jessica Levesque, MaineCare’s project lead, with questions related to this rate determination process.

This notice is sent pursuant to Rate Reform law.
